ov: A small freshwater fish from north-east South America that gives birth to live young. Males are smaller and splashed with bright colours; females are grey. Released on every continent except Antarctica, it is one of the most widespread tropical fish and a very popular aquarium fish.

why.p: One of the most popular freshwater aquarium fish.
why.dm: Breeders have produced many fancy strains, bigger and more colourful than wild guppies.

rg: Native to Venezuela, Guyana, Brazil, Trinidad and Tobago, Barbados and Antigua; introduced to countries on every continent except Antarctica.
df: Algae, diatoms, small invertebrates, insect larvae, plant bits and detritus. Algae are usually the biggest part.
fx: Females can first give birth at just 10–20 weeks old.
Guppies from streams with many predators school more than those from safe streams.
